scenario.title: Context switch bug - PendSV forgets to save and restore r8
scenario.description: The PendSV handler's register list is {r4-r7, r9-r11} instead of {r4-r11}. Nothing faults. Task A keeps a value in r8, stores what it expects, runs a delay loop (so a tick lands inside it), and compares r8 afterwards. Task B also uses r8 for its own counter. After the first switch A -> B -> A, task A finds B's r8 in its register and records a corruption. The scenario shows how a missing register in the software frame surfaces as data corruption far from the handler.

expected.summary: No faults, tasks keep switching, but task A reports r8 corruptions (marker events) and the "corruptions" global is non-zero.

scenario.what_to_look_for: The scenario event lists the injected fault. The kernel's PendSV source in this run uses stmdb/ldmia with a seven-register list; the context_switch events look normal (PSPs change, nothing faults). Then, soon after the first switch back to A, a marker event "taskA: r8 corrupted after a context switch". The global "corruptions" counts how often it happened; a_iters is reset each time. Compare with P06 where the same task set with a complete register list never reports a corruption. In the viewer, click the context_switch events: the saved frame on A's stack has only seven words before the hardware frame, so the PSP in the TCB is off by four relative to the correct layout.
likely_root_causes: A register missing from the stmdb/ldmia list in the PendSV handler (classic: r8 or r11, because the list was typed as r4-r7, r9-r11 or copied from an example that used a different set).
The compiler uses a register the switch does not save (a kernel written in C with a naked handler and the wrong clobber list).
Saving with one register order and restoring with another, so the values go back into the wrong registers.
FPU context: if the FPU is enabled, s16-s31 also need saving (lazy stacking).
how_to_debug: Write a GDB script that breaks in PendSV, prints the PSP and 16 words above it, and compares to the stack-layout diagram; count the words before the hardware frame (must be 8).
In each task, keep a known constant in r8-r11 (register variables) and check it after every delay; the first task to see a wrong value points at the register.
Review the handler's register list against the ABI table: r4-r11 are callee-saved and must be in the software frame, r0-r3/r12/lr/pc/xPSR are already in the hardware frame.
Run two tasks with different values in the suspect register and dump both TCB frames: the missing word shifts everything below it.
scenario.what_this_means: A context switch must preserve every register the ABI calls callee-saved, because the task was interrupted at an arbitrary instruction and expects all of them intact. Missing one does not fault; it leaks one task's value into another, intermittently, only when a tick happens while the register is live. That is why the course asks for a stack-layout diagram before any switch code is written.
scenario.hidden_symptom: Tasks run, but one of them occasionally computes garbage or resets its counter; nothing in the fault log.
